Psychosis Metabolic Risk Calculator

Understand early.Act together.Live healthier.

We built PsyMetRiC, a regulated clinical prediction tool, to estimate the risk of clinically significant weight gain, metabolic syndrome and type 2 diabetes in people aged 16 to 35 with psychosis. PsyMetRiC was developed hand in hand with stakeholders, including people with experience of psychosis, carers and health professionals. PsyMetRiC has been validated using data from over 25,000 people with early psychosis in the UK, and has been separately validated in 9 countries across four continents.

Open the calculator Watch how it works
MHRA Class I Medical Device For people with early psychosis aged 16 to 35 years Uses routine clinical data Suitable for secondary mental health services and primary care

Why it matters

Physical health is often sidelined when prevention matters most

Signs of cardiometabolic risk can appear from the onset of psychosis, which occurs most often in early adulthood. Physical healthcare in this group is too often reactive, waiting for physical health problems to emerge before offering treatment. PsyMetRiC changes that, giving patients and health professionals a shared understanding of risk, toward collaborative decision-making around prevention.

Agree prevention together

Clear visuals help the young person and health professional understand the physical health risk together and agree the next step, such as health behaviour support, a medication review or closer monitoring.

Prevention in everyday life

Understand early. Act together. Live healthier.

Shared understanding of physical health risk

Physical health risk you can understand together

Most clinical prediction tools stop at a number. We co-produced PsyMetRiC with young people, carers and health professionals so that both sides of the conversation understand the result. This focus on shared understanding has rarely been done before, and we believe it gives young people more say in their own care.

Uncertaintya likely range, not false precision
Change over timehow physical health risk may rise in the years ahead
What drives itthe factors pushing the risk score higher, and pulling it lower
A similar individualcompare physical health risk with someone of a similar background but different physical health risk factors
Metabolic agean easy way into the conversation

Who it is for

One tool, four conversations

Mental health teams and GPs

Protect physical health from the first consultation, without adding to your workload

  • Early: see metabolic risk before physical health problems emerge
  • Long term: agree a collaborative prevention plan that prioritises physical as well as mental health
  • Light touch: inputs can be pre-filled from the electronic health record

NHS and policy leaders

In line with the NHS 10 Year Plan, we bring prevention, community and digital care together in one mental health care workflow

  • Sickness to prevention: act on metabolic risk before costly, life-shortening illness
  • Hospital to community: mental health teams act early and the GP hand-over carries the plan
  • Analogue to digital: metabolic risk scored from your patient record, inside the NHS boundary

Budget holders and commissioners

Focus prevention where it may matter most

We designed PsyMetRiC to help services use prevention resources well:

  • Uses information that teams already record, so it fits routine care
  • Helps identify young people at higher metabolic risk before physical health problems emerge
  • Supports referral to health behavioural and other prevention support for those likely to benefit most
  • Licensed per service, with a proposal tailored to local capacity

Young people and the people who support them

Your physical health matters from the start. An understandable physical health risk estimate empowers you and your team to plan collaboratively.

  • You may look and feel well, but your physical health risk can still be high
  • Your result is a starting point for a conversation, not a judgement
  • You choose the steps that fit your life, with support from your team

9 countries across 4 continentsPsyMetRiC is extensively tested around the world
A trusted medical devicePsyMetRiC is a regulated medical device with the MHRA
16 to 35designed for the age group where general tools are least accurate
The Lester Positive Cardiometabolic Health ResourcePsyMetRiC forms part of the NHS England co-produced Lester Positive Cardiometabolic Health Resource
In useapproved for use in Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust

Built for the years when psychosis often begins

We built PsyMetRiC for individuals aged 16 to 35, the age range when psychosis tends to emerge in most people. Three in four people with schizophrenia first show symptoms by age 35.

About us

About PsyMetRiCOur team

About PsyMetRiC

Young people with psychosis deserve the same chance of a long, healthy life as anyone else.

We began as a research project. Today PsyMetRiC is a trusted, regulated medical device used in clinics, and we aim to make it a service that NHS organisations adopt. We are the PsyMetRiC Operating Division at University of Birmingham Enterprise.

Research toolWhere we began
Trusted, regulated medical deviceReady for use in clinics today
NHS serviceWhere we are heading

Brand essence

Why we exist and where we are going

Purpose

Young people with psychosis deserve the same chance of a long, healthy life as anyone else.

Vision

PsyMetRiC-guided prevention in every NHS psychosis early intervention service, GP practice, and beyond.

Mission

Help young people with psychosis protect their physical health from the very start of care, through shared risk understanding and collaborative decision-making.

Promise

A shared understanding of physical health risk, built from routine data, so that young people and health professionals can work in partnership to protect physical health from the very start of care.

Our values

Four values guide what we do

Evidence first

We say what the data show, with sources and limits.

Co-produced

Built with stakeholders including young people with experience of psychosis, carers and health professionals; their words shape ours.

Equitable

Designed to narrow health gaps across ethnic and social groups.

Practical

Fits real clinics: quick, clear and useful in a conversation.

We are

TrustedClearHopefulCaringRigorous

We are not

What our logo expresses

Seen as a whole person. Heard as an equal.

Every PsyMetRiC conversation begins with two people. Our logo was created by a group of people with lived experience of psychosis.

A conversation between equals. A young person and a health professional sit side by side. Both voices are valued, with space to speak and be heard.

Mind and body connected. The dark circles over the brain and heart reflect the link between mental and physical wellbeing.

Connection through conversation. The dots are the words, questions and hopes shared in conversation.

Warm and welcoming. Bright, gentle colours made to resonate with young people and bring warmth to clinical settings.

From journal to clinic: how PsyMetRiC reached real-world care

Dr Ben Perry, Associate Clinical Professor of Psychiatry and founder of PsyMetRiC, explains why much prediction research stays in journals, and how working with University of Birmingham Enterprise helped PsyMetRiC become a tool used in clinical practice.

Join us at the EIP Forum

A short teaching session for early intervention teams in Birmingham and Solihull: why physical health matters from the first episode, and how PsyMetRiC fits the shared physical health protocol.

News · ServiceComing soon

LiveWell clinic opens to young people in early intervention

LiveWell offers preventive lifestyle support, including exercise, nutrition, smoking cessation and peer support. Young people whose PsyMetRiC score shows raised physical health risk can be referred by their care team.

News · GuidanceDate to be announced

PsyMetRiC named in the Lester resource

The Lester positive cardiometabolic health resource recommends PsyMetRiC for assessing physical health risk in people with psychosis aged 35 and under.
